So with sharing enabled, a team credential (userId null) gets a direct OAuth response parsed by the minimum schema, which sets `refresh_token` to the literal placeholder "refresh_token" and drops other fields — corrupting stored credentials. Salesforce calls parseRefreshTokenResponse with salesforceTokenSchema but never goes through ref

So with sharing enabled, a team credential (userId null) gets a direct OAuth response parsed by the minimum schema, which sets `refresh_token` to the literal placeholder "refresh_token" and drops other fields — corrupting stored credentials. Salesforce calls parseRefreshTokenResponse with salesforceTokenSchema but never goes through refreshOAuthTokens, yet when sharing is enabled its real response is parsed against the minimum schema and stored (`key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }`) losing instance_url/signature/issued_at. The mechanism matches the diff exactly.

judged_text: Schema selection is keyed only on APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, but the response passed in only originates from the sync endpoint when userId is truthy (refreshOAuthTokens' extra gate) or when the app uses refreshOAuthTokens at all (salesforce never does), so direct-OAuth responses get parsed with the minimum sync schema. Team-scoped credentials (userId null) for office365-calendar/zoom get their real refresh_token overwritten with the 'refresh_token' placeholder and their expiry stripped on first refresh, so the next direct refresh authenticates with a fake token and the credential is bricked; in sync mode salesforce's stored key loses instance_url/issued_at/signature, breaking subsequent jsforce connections.
